_comment: UNI-237. Reviewed exemptions from scripts/lint-pattern-breadth.js. Each entry needs a pattern and a reason. A stale entry (technology or pattern gone) and a no-op entry (no longer over threshold) both FAIL the build -- this list may not accumulate dead weight.

Bootstrap.reason: UNI-237 known gap: "bootstrap" is itself an entry in patterns/dictionary.txt (a real English word for a boot-pulling loop), so the specificity screen cannot distinguish it from ordinary prose. But Bootstrap-the-framework is literally named after that word, so its `bootstrap` pattern is a legitimate, low-noise signal (excess is only 14% of the technology's own fires, well under the 25% relative line -- it fails on the absolute test alone, at 3803 total fires across the corpus). Reviewed and kept; Bootstrap's genuinely over-broad patterns (class=".*row", class=".*col-", class=".*btn-") are NOT exempted and remain violations.

Vue.js.reason: UNI-237: flagged only because 'data' is a dictionary word; the compound 'data-v-' (with trailing hyphen requiring a following scope hash) is Vue's actual scoped-style attribute syntax. Sole evidence path (strongest=0) -- both sampled matches were genuine Vue markers (data-v-app root marker, [data-v-<hash>] scoped CSS selector). Deleting it would leave Vue.js undetectable.

WordPress.reason: UNI-237: flagged only because 'content' is a dictionary word; 'wp-content' is WordPress's literal install-directory path, not prose. Fails the absolute test alone (8% excess of its own 1650 fires) -- it is the single most reliable WordPress marker in the corpus, corroborated by 1485 independent (meta generator) hits already.

EAB Navigate.reason: UNI-237: flagged because 'navigate' is a dictionary word, but empirically precise -- 10+/15 sampled hits were genuine *.navigate.eab.com subdomains or 'EAB Navigate'/'Navigate360' product text. Catches the navigate.eab.com subdomain that the existing literal campus.eab.com/bouncer.eab.com patterns miss.

UNI-237: same product, reverse token order; ~8/15 sampled hits were genuine *.navigate.eab.com links (frontrange, k-state, frostburg, dallascollege, cc-chicago). Non-redundant with campus.eab.com/bouncer.eab.com, which do not cover this subdomain.

Workday Student.reason: UNI-237: flagged as a bare dictionary word, but a 15-sample check found ~13/15 genuine *.myworkdayjobs.com / *.workday.com / workday.<edu> career-portal links; only 1/15 was ordinary prose. Sole detection path for the many distinct wdN.myworkdayjobs.com subdomains that the narrower workday\\.com / wd5\\.myworkday\\.com literals do not cover.

Stimulus.reason: UNI-237: flagged because 'data' and 'controller' are both dictionary words, but data-controller is Stimulus's defining HTML attribute -- not a phrase that occurs in ordinary prose. Sole evidence path (strongest=0); sampled hits are genuine data-controller="..." attributes from Stimulus-powered form widgets.

Concept3D.reason: UNI-237: flagged only because 'concept' is a dictionary word; the digit-suffixed compound 'concept3d' is a unique brand token. 12/12 sampled hits were genuine map.concept3d.com / tour.concept3d.com URLs -- 100% precision.

W3 Total Cache.reason: UNI-237: flagged because 'total' and 'cache' are dictionary words, but this is the literal, verbatim HTML comment the W3 Total Cache plugin inserts on every page it optimizes ("Performance optimized by W3 Total Cache..."). Sole evidence path (strongest=0) alongside the X-Powered-By header; not a prose collision, an anchored vendor string.

Alpine.js.reason: UNI-237: flagged because 'data' is a dictionary word; x-data is Alpine.js's defining directive attribute. Sole evidence path (strongest=0); 11/12 sampled hits were genuine x-data="..." attributes, the one false hit a coincidental 'lightbox-dataContainer' class-name boundary artifact.

WordPress Super Cache.reason: UNI-237: flagged because 'super' and 'cache' are dictionary words, but this is the literal HTML footer comment the WP Super Cache plugin inserts ("Cached page generated by WP-Super-Cache on ..."). Sole evidence path alongside the WP-Super-Cache header; anchored vendor string, not prose.

Element451.reason: UNI-237: flagged only because 'element' is a dictionary word; the digit-suffixed compound 'element451' is a unique brand token (a Fahrenheit-451 reference). 11/12 sampled hits were genuine (wp-content/plugins/element451-integration, shell.451.io script tags, "Element451 Chatbox" comment).

Ellucian Colleague.reason: UNI-237: flagged because 'colleague' is a dictionary word, but every sampled hit was a genuine *.colleague.elluciancloud.com portal URL. Non-redundant with the existing 'ellucian[^>]*colleague' pattern, which requires the reverse token order and misses this (very common) URL form where 'colleague' precedes 'elluciancloud'.
UNI-237: same vendor, all sampled hits genuine *.colleague.elluciancloud.com / elluciancrmrecruit.com URLs across many institutions.

Blackboard Learn.reason: UNI-237: flagged because 'blackboard' and 'learn' are both dictionary words, but sampled hits were all genuine ("Blackboard Learn with the Ultra Experience", plain "Blackboard Learn" menu labels, blackboard.com login links) -- text-only product-name mentions that the literal 'blackboard\\.com' pattern does not cover.

CollegeNET 25Live.reason: UNI-237: flagged only because the token happens to end in the dictionary word 'live'; the leading digit makes '25live' a distinctive compressed brand name, not English prose. All sampled hits were genuine 25livepub.collegenet.com / 25live.collegenet.com URLs and cookie names.

Shibboleth.reason: UNI-237: 'shibboleth' is a legitimate (archaic) English dictionary word, but it essentially never appears in ordinary HE marketing prose -- both sampled hits were genuine SSO login paths (idm.suny.edu/shibboleth/idp/, .../sso/shibboleth/...). Low volume (13 matches), high precision.
vendor-anchored: 'shib' is not a dictionary word, so the wildcard's dictionary-word half ('session') is incidental -- 'shib' alone already anchors this to Shibboleth SSO.

Localist.reason: UNI-237 (gate re-run 2026-08-11, after event.*calendar was removed): 'localist' is in the dictionary (one who advocates localism), but it is Localist's own vendor name and its primary marker. 8/8 sampled hits were genuine (localist-widget CSS classes, localist_widget_container, localist-images.azureedge.net CDN) -- markup and asset URLs, not prose.

25Live.reason: UNI-237 (gate re-run 2026-08-11, after event.*management was removed): tokenises to the dictionary word 'live', but the leading digit makes '25live' the distinctive product name, not prose. 8/8 sampled hits were genuine 25livepub.collegenet.com / 25live.collegenet.com URLs and the '25Live' menu label.

Blackboard Ultra.reason: UNI-237 (gate re-run 2026-08-11, after bb.*ultra and the unbounded blackboard.*ultra were tightened/removed): both tokens are ordinary words and 'Blackboard' does appear in unrelated LMS prose, so this was checked directly rather than assumed vendor-specific. All 19 matches at this bound are markup or URL/config, never a prose sentence -- menu labels ("Blackboard Ultra"), blackboard.com/ultra and help.blackboard.com/Learn/Student/Ultra links, SSO redirectUrl query-string paths, and one calendar-event description field. Kept because the evidence is structural, not narrative.

Kaltura.reason: vendor-anchored: 'kaltura' is not a dictionary word and is a distinctive vendor token; 'player' on the other side is incidental. Sampled hits were genuine (@playkit-js/kaltura-player-js style IDs).

Parchment.reason: UNI-237: 'parchment' is a dictionary word (paper), but 11/12 sampled hits were genuine parchment.com transcript-request links; only 1/12 was ordinary prose ("Duplicate parchments"). Sole evidence path (strongest=0) -- deleting it would leave Parchment undetectable.
